examples.ko: 시험에 떨어진 뒤로 계속 의기소침해 있어요.
examples.en: I've been feeling down ever since I failed the exam.
Why do you look so down today?
One word from my friend left me discouraged.

examples.ko: 너무 의기소침하지 말고 다시 한번 해 봐요.
examples.en: Don't be too discouraged, try one more time.

examples.ko: 발표를 망쳐서 하루 종일 의기소침한 얼굴이었어요.
examples.en: I messed up my presentation and looked dejected all day.

examples.ko: 아이가 의기소침할 때는 따뜻하게 안아 주세요.
examples.en: When your child is feeling down, give them a warm hug.

explain: '우울하다'보다 가벼운 말로, 실패하거나 지적을 받아서 자신감이 떨어지고 기운이 없을 때 써요. 반대말은 '의기양양하다'예요. 일상 대화에서는 '기가 죽다'라고도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It is lighter than '우울하다' (gloomy) and is used when you lose confidence and energy after a failure or criticism. Its opposite is '의기양양하다'. In everyday talk people also often say '기가 죽다'.

examples.en: The winning players walked out looking triumphant.
My younger sibling is full of pride after getting 100 on the test.
He received the prize with a triumphant look.
He was so full of himself, and he ended up making a mistake.

examples.ko: 칭찬을 한 번 들었다고 너무 의기양양해졌어요.
examples.en: You got way too cocky just because you heard one compliment.

examples.ko: 의기양양할 때일수록 말과 행동을 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: The prouder you feel, the more careful you should be with your words and actions.

explain: 성공하거나 칭찬받아서 자랑스러운 마음이 겉으로 드러날 때 써요. 보통 '의기양양하게', '의기양양한 표정'처럼 모습을 설명할 때 많이 나와요. 반대말은 '의기소침하다'예요.
explain_en: It is used when pride from success or praise shows on the outside. It mostly appears in forms like '의기양양하게' or '의기양양한 표정' to describe someone's look. Its opposite is '의기소침하다'.

en: be of one mind; hit it off

examples.ko: 두 사람은 처음 만난 날부터 의기투합했어요.
examples.en: The two of them clicked from the day they first met.
We share a hobby, so we hit it off quickly.
The team members came together and achieved great results.
I opened a shop with friends who shared my vision.
People with similar ideas easily hit it off.
The two hit it off and then set up a company together.

explain: '마음이 맞다'와 비슷하지만, 뜻이 통해서 함께 무언가를 해 보자는 느낌이 강해요. '~와 의기투합하다', '~끼리 의기투합하다'로 써요. 그냥 사이가 좋다는 뜻은 아니에요.
explain_en: It is similar to '마음이 맞다' (to be on the same wavelength), but it strongly suggests people agreeing and deciding to do something together. It is used as '~와 의기투합하다' or '~끼리 의기투합하다'. It does not simply mean getting along well.

examples.ko: 많은 사람들이 그 발표의 정확성을 의문시해요.
examples.en: Many people question the accuracy of that announcement.

examples.ko: 전문가들은 이 계획의 효과를 의문시하고 있어요.
examples.en: Experts are doubting the effectiveness of this plan.

examples.ko: 저는 그의 말을 의문시한 적이 없어요.
examples.en: I have never doubted what he said.
Nobody questioned the result.
At first, everyone doubted the chance of success.
The reporter asked questions, doubting the government's explanation.

explain: '의심하다'보다 딱딱해서 뉴스나 글에서 많이 나와요. '~을/를 의문시하다'로 쓰고, 일상 대화에서는 '의심하다'나 '못 믿겠다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It sounds stiffer than '의심하다' and appears often in news and writing. It is used as '~을/를 의문시하다', while in daily conversation people say '의심하다' or '못 믿겠다'.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 의뭉스러워서 속마음을 알 수 없어요.
examples.en: He is sly, so I can't tell what he really thinks.
The way he smiles so slyly looks a bit suspicious.
My younger sibling came out of the room with a sly look.
He pretends not to know, but he looks sly.
My grandfather is often told that he is crafty.
Stop being sly and tell me honestly.

explain: 속으로는 다 알면서 겉으로는 모르는 척하는 능청스러운 느낌이에요. 칭찬하는 말은 아니고, 속셈이 있어 보인다는 느낌이 들어요. 주로 '의뭉스러운 사람/표정'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It gives the feeling of someone who knows everything inside but acts as if they know nothing. It is not a compliment and suggests a hidden agenda. It is mostly used like '의뭉스러운 사람' or '의뭉스러운 표정'.

examples.en: He gave a meaningful smile.
The teacher's words sounded really profound to me.
The last scene of this movie is full of meaning.
His look was so loaded that it bothered me.

examples.ko: 의미심장하게 쳐다보더니 아무 말도 안 했어요.
examples.en: He gave me a meaningful look and said nothing.

examples.ko: 이 사건이 의미심장한 변화의 시작일지도 몰라요.
examples.en: This incident may be the start of a significant change.

explain: 말, 표정, 장면 속에 숨은 뜻이 있어 보일 때 써요. '의미 있다'는 가치가 있다는 느낌이 강하고, '의미심장하다'는 깊은 속뜻이 있어 보인다는 느낌이에요. 보통 '의미심장한 말/미소/눈빛'으로 써요.
explain_en: It is used when a word, expression or scene seems to hide a deeper meaning. '의미 있다' stresses that something has value, while '의미심장하다' suggests a deep hidden meaning. It is usually used as '의미심장한 말/미소/눈빛'.

examples.en: I get along very well with my stepfather.
My stepfather took me to school.
That child calls his stepfather 'Dad'.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 의붓아버지 덕분에 큰 도움을 받았어요.
examples.en: When I was young, I got a lot of help thanks to my stepfather.
My stepfather devotes himself to his new family.
My friend's stepfather is really good at cooking.

explain: 어머니가 재혼해서 생긴 아버지를 말해요. 직접 부를 때는 '의붓아버지'라고 하지 않고 '아버지', '아빠'라고 불러요. 글이나 서류에서는 '계부'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It refers to the father you gain when your mother remarries. When addressing him directly, people don't say '의붓아버지' but call him '아버지' or '아빠'. In writing or documents it is also called '계부'.

examples.en: My stepmother and I are like friends.
My stepmother packs me a lunch box every day.
She calls her stepmother 'Mom'.
My stepmother took care of my birthday.
My stepmother treats me like her own daughter.
I learned cooking from my stepmother when I was young.

explain: 아버지가 재혼해서 생긴 어머니를 말해요. 직접 부를 때는 '어머니', '엄마'라고 해요. '새어머니'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It refers to the mother you gain when your father remarries. When addressing her directly, people say '어머니' or '엄마'. It is also called '새어머니'.

examples.en: He raised his stepchild just like his own child.
You must not discriminate against a child for being a stepchild.

examples.ko: 그 부부는 의붓자식 셋을 함께 돌보고 있어요.
examples.en: That couple is raising three stepchildren together.
She is someone who embraced her stepchild with love.
A stepchild appears as the main character in the drama.
That woman was always warm to her stepchild as well.

explain: 배우자가 데려온 아이, 즉 재혼한 상대의 자식을 말해요. 아들과 딸을 나누어 '의붓아들', '의붓딸'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It refers to the child your spouse brings into a marriage, that is, the child of your remarried partner. By gender it can be '의붓아들' (stepson) or '의붓딸' (stepdaughter).

examples.en: I took photos with my friends in front of the assembly hall.
There is a very large assembly building in Yeouido.
The lawmakers gathered at the assembly hall and began the meeting.
On our school trip we went to Seoul and toured the assembly building.

examples.ko: 의사당 건물은 밖에서 보면 정말 웅장해요.
examples.en: The assembly building looks really grand from the outside.
I took a walk in a park near the assembly hall.

explain: 우리나라에서는 보통 '국회의사당'이라고 해요. 그냥 '의사당'은 의회가 모여 일하는 건물을 말해요. 병원의 '의사'와는 관계가 없는 말이에요.
explain_en: In Korea people usually say '국회의사당' (National Assembly building). '의사당' alone means the building where a legislature meets. It has nothing to do with '의사' (doctor).

examples.ko: 이번 선거에서 그 당의 의석수가 크게 늘었어요.
examples.en: In this election, that party's number of seats grew a lot.

examples.ko: 의석수가 많은 정당이 법안을 통과시키기 쉬워요.
examples.en: A party with many seats can pass bills more easily.
The two parties have almost the same number of seats.
The negotiations dragged on over the number of seats.
The ruling party tried hard to keep its seats.
The party leader resigned because the seat count fell.

explain: 선거 뉴스에서 자주 나오는 말이에요. '의석'은 자리 하나하나를, '의석수'는 그 개수를 말해요. '의석을 얻다/잃다/차지하다'처럼 '의석'과 함께 알아 두면 좋아요.
explain_en: It appears often in election news. '의석' is each individual seat, and '의석수' is the count of them. It helps to learn it together with '의석' in phrases like '의석을 얻다/잃다/차지하다'.

examples.ko: 이 캠페인은 환경 문제를 의식화하려는 목적으로 만들었어요.
examples.en: This campaign was made with the aim of raising awareness of environmental problems.

examples.ko: 그 모임은 시민들을 의식화하는 활동을 해요.
examples.en: That group carries out activities to raise citizens' awareness.
Only when you become conscious of the problem can you see solutions.

examples.ko: 무의식 속 생각을 의식화해 말로 해 보세요.
examples.en: Bring the thoughts in your unconscious to awareness and try to say them in words.
The film was praised as one that raised awareness of discrimination.

examples.ko: 아이들을 특정 생각으로 의식화하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not indoctrinate children with one particular idea.

explain: 막연하던 것을 뚜렷하게 알아차리게 만든다는 느낌으로, 사회 문제나 심리 이야기에서 써요. 남을 특정한 생각으로 이끈다는 부정적인 느낌으로 쓰일 때도 있어요. 'A를 의식화하다'로 써요.
explain_en: It carries the sense of making something vague clearly noticed, and is used in talk about social issues or psychology. It can also have a negative feel, meaning to steer others toward a particular idea. It is used as 'A를 의식화하다'.

examples.en: His sudden words made me wonder.
I couldn't hide my puzzlement and asked back.

examples.ko: 아무도 없는데 소리가 나서 의아심이 생겼어요.
examples.en: A sound came though nobody was there, and it puzzled me.
My friend looked at me with a face full of puzzlement.
Puzzled, I asked him directly.
I looked up several things to clear up my doubts.

explain: '의아심이 들다/생기다', '의아심을 품다'처럼 써요. '의심'은 믿지 못하는 느낌이고, '의아심'은 이상해서 고개를 갸웃하는 느낌이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '이상하다', '왜 그러지?'라고 말하는 일이 많아요.
explain_en: It is used in phrases like '의아심이 들다/생기다' and '의아심을 품다'. '의심' is not believing something, while '의아심' is the puzzled feeling of finding something strange. In daily talk people often just say '이상하다' or '왜 그러지?'.

examples.ko: 그는 큰 병 앞에서도 의연하게 행동했어요.
examples.en: He acted composedly even in the face of a serious illness.
His steady manner put everyone at ease.
My mother stayed strong even in her sorrow.
The way you handle it calmly is admirable.

examples.ko: 비난에도 의연할 수 있는 사람이 되고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to be a person who can stay firm even under criticism.
I tried to look composed, but my hands were shaking.

explain: 어려운 일이나 슬픔 앞에서도 흔들리지 않고 침착한 태도를 말해요. 사람의 태도를 좋게 말할 때 써요. '의젓하다'와 비슷하지만 '의연하다'는 위기나 슬픔 속의 태도에 더 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It describes staying steady and calm in the face of hardship or sorrow, and is used as praise for a person's attitude. It is similar to '의젓하다', but '의연하다' fits better for one's attitude in a crisis or in grief.

examples.en: He accepted even the hard verdict calmly.
My mother got up firmly and looked after the children.
You have to face a crisis with composure.
Even after losing, the player greeted everyone with composure.

examples.ko: 의연히 앞을 보며 걸어가는 모습이 멋졌어요.
examples.en: The way he walked on, looking steadily ahead, was cool.

examples.ko: 오랜 세월이 지나도 마을 입구의 나무는 의연히 그대로예요.
examples.en: Even after many years, the tree at the village entrance remains just as it was.

explain: 주로 글이나 뉴스에서 쓰고, 말할 때는 '의연하게'가 더 자연스러워요. 침착하고 흔들림 없이라는 뜻 외에, 예문처럼 '예전과 다름없이'라는 뜻으로도 쓰여요.
explain_en: It is mostly used in writing or news, and '의연하게' sounds more natural in speech. Besides 'calmly and without wavering', it can also mean 'just as before', as in the last example.

examples.en: I entered the pre-med course at university this year.
After finishing pre-med, you move up to the medical program.
My younger sibling studies hard to get into pre-med.

examples.ko: 의예과 학생들은 기초 과목을 많이 들어요.
examples.en: Pre-med students take many basic courses.
Admission to pre-med is extremely competitive.
My friend is in pre-med, so they're always busy.

explain: 의과대학에서 본격적인 의학 공부 전에 다니는 첫 과정이에요. 일상에서는 '의대'라고 줄여 말하는 경우가 많은데, '의예과'는 학과 이름이고 '의대'는 단과대학이에요.
explain_en: It is the first stage of a medical college, before the main medical studies. In daily talk people often just say '의대', but '의예과' is the name of the program while '의대' is the college itself.

examples.en: He cut ties with his older brother over a money issue.
I've cut off my parents and live alone.
It hurts that I've broken off with an old friend.
It's been over ten years since we cut ties.
Even if you're angry, don't cut off your family.

examples.ko: 두 사람은 크게 다투고 의절해 버렸어요.
examples.en: The two had a big fight and ended up cutting ties.

explain: 가족이나 친척, 아주 가까운 사이와 관계를 끊는다는 무거운 말이에요. '~와/과 의절하다'로 써요. 단순히 연락이 뜸해진 정도가 아니에요. 친구 사이에는 '절교하다'도 써요.
explain_en: It is a heavy word for cutting off a relationship with family, relatives or very close people, used as '~와/과 의절하다'. It is more than just losing touch. Between friends, '절교하다' is also used.

examples.en: Dependence on smartphones is steadily increasing.

examples.ko: 의존성이 강한 아이는 혼자 결정하기 어려워해요.
examples.en: A child with strong dependency has trouble deciding alone.

examples.ko: 이 약은 의존성이 생길 수 있어서 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: This medicine can cause dependence, so you need to be careful.
Our country has a high reliance on imports.
To become an adult, you need to reduce dependence.
I received counseling because of my dependence on games.

explain: '의존'이 기대는 일 자체라면 '의존성'은 그런 성질이나 정도를 말해요. '높다/낮다, 강하다, 줄이다'와 함께 쓰고, 걱정스러운 문제를 이야기할 때 많이 나와요.
explain_en: While '의존' is the act of relying, '의존성' refers to that tendency or its degree. It goes with words like '높다/낮다', '강하다' and '줄이다', and often appears when talking about worrying problems.

examples.en: The two sisters get along really well.
I read the story of the loving brothers.
My parents always live in harmony.
They are neighbors known as a loving couple.
The brothers are close, which is nice to see.
The classmates cleaned up together in a friendly way.

explain: 주로 '의좋게 지내다', '의좋은 형제/부부'처럼 써요. 형제, 부부, 친구처럼 가까운 사이에 어울리고, 일상 대화에서는 '사이가 좋다'가 더 흔해요. '의가 좋다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is mostly used in forms like '의좋게 지내다' and '의좋은 형제/부부'. It suits close relationships such as siblings, couples and friends, while '사이가 좋다' is more common in daily talk. It can also be said '의가 좋다'.

examples.en: I can't tell what the other person has in mind.
I wonder what the boss really has in mind.
I asked a question to sound out his intentions.

examples.ko: 말은 안 했지만 의중은 분명해 보였어요.
examples.en: He didn't say it, but his intention seemed clear.
I revised the report to match the team leader's thinking.
He hid his real intentions and only smiled.

explain: 마음속에 품은 생각을 말하는데, 특히 일이나 결정에 대한 속뜻에 많이 써요. '의중을 파악하다/떠보다/헤아리다'처럼 쓰고, 윗사람이나 상대방의 생각을 말할 때 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It refers to the thought someone holds inside, especially their true intention about a task or decision. It is used in phrases like '의중을 파악하다/떠보다/헤아리다' and often appears when talking about a superior's or the other party's thinking.

examples.en: My grandfather puts in his dentures before meals.

examples.ko: 의치가 잘 맞지 않아서 치과에 갔어요.
examples.en: The denture didn't fit well, so I went to the dentist.

examples.ko: 어머니는 밤에 의치를 빼서 물에 담가 두세요.
examples.en: My mother takes out her dentures at night and soaks them in water.

examples.ko: 의치 때문에 딱딱한 음식은 먹기 힘들어요.
examples.en: Because of the dentures, hard food is difficult to eat.

examples.ko: 새 의치를 맞추는 데 일주일쯤 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes about a week to get new dentures made.

examples.ko: 의치를 하고 나서 발음이 조금 달라졌어요.
examples.en: After getting dentures, my pronunciation changed a little.

explain: 일상에서는 '틀니'라고 훨씬 많이 말해요. '의치'는 병원이나 글에서 쓰는 조금 격식 있는 말이에요. 빠진 이를 대신하는 인공 치아를 가리켜요.
explain_en: In daily life people say '틀니' much more often. '의치' is a slightly formal word used at hospitals and in writing. It refers to artificial teeth that replace missing ones.

en: turn to; depend on; fall back on

examples.en: I had nowhere to go, so I relied on a relative.

examples.ko: 그는 노후를 자식에게 의탁하고 싶어 하지 않아요.
examples.en: He doesn't want to depend on his children in old age.
We decided to leave the child in the care of my uncle's home.
Many people also lean on religion for their hearts.

examples.ko: 남에게만 의탁하지 말고 스스로 일어서야 해요.
examples.en: Don't rely only on others; you need to stand on your own.
My grandmother lives, putting herself in the care of a temple.

explain: 몸이나 마음, 생활을 남에게 맡기고 기대는 것으로, '~에게 몸을 의탁하다'처럼 써요. '의지하다'보다 완전히 맡긴다는 느낌이 있고, 말보다 글에서 더 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It means leaving your body, mind or livelihood to someone else and leaning on them, as in '~에게 몸을 의탁하다'. It feels more like handing yourself over completely than '의지하다', and appears more in writing than in speech.

examples.ko: 이 연구는 의학계에서 큰 관심을 받았어요.
examples.en: This study received great attention in the medical world.
The medical community evaluated the new treatment cautiously.

examples.ko: 의학계의 의견이 아직 하나로 모이지 않았어요.
examples.en: Opinion in the medical world has not yet come together.
He is a professor respected in the medical field.
New news reached the medical world.
People working in medicine gathered and held a discussion.

explain: '~계'는 어떤 분야에 있는 사람들 전체를 가리켜요. 정치계, 교육계, 학계처럼 쓰고, 의학계는 의사와 연구자 등 의학 분야 사람들을 두루 말해요. 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '~계' refers to all the people in a certain field, as in 정치계, 교육계 and 학계. '의학계' broadly means the people in medicine, such as doctors and researchers. It appears often in the news.

examples.ko: 그는 의협심이 강해서 약한 사람을 도와요.
examples.en: He has a strong sense of chivalry, so he helps the weak.
Out of a chivalrous spirit, I stepped into the fight.
The boy showed his gallantry and saved his friend.
I want to be a person with a chivalrous heart.
I'm proud of my older brother, who is full of chivalry.
Burning with a sense of justice, he chased after the thief.

explain: 정의감과 비슷하지만, 어려운 사람을 직접 나서서 돕는 용감한 마음이라는 느낌이 더 강해요. '의협심이 강하다/있다/넘치다', '의협심을 발휘하다'로 써요.
explain_en: It is similar to a sense of justice, but it feels more like a brave heart that steps forward to help people in trouble. It is used as '의협심이 강하다/있다/넘치다' and '의협심을 발휘하다'.

examples.en: The two of them are sworn brothers.
He cherishes his old friend like a brother.
It's already been twenty years since we became sworn brothers.
We promised to become sworn brothers.

examples.ko: 의형제 사이라 서로 속마음을 다 알아요.
examples.en: We're sworn brothers, so we know each other's real feelings.

examples.ko: 영화 속 의형제가 눈물 나게 했어요.
examples.en: The sworn brothers in the movie made me cry.

explain: 피가 섞이지 않았지만 형제처럼 지내기로 약속한 사이를 말해요. '의형제를 맺다'라는 표현으로 많이 써요. 실제 형제를 말하는 '친형제'와 달라요.
explain_en: It refers to people who aren't related by blood but have agreed to be like brothers. It is commonly used in the phrase '의형제를 맺다'. It differs from '친형제', which means real siblings.

en: sowing discord; setting people against each other

examples.ko: 그 사람의 이간질 때문에 사이가 멀어졌어요.
examples.en: We grew apart because of that person's meddling.
Don't be fooled by the sowing of discord; ask directly.

examples.ko: 회사에서 이간질을 하는 사람이 제일 싫어요.
examples.en: I hate people who turn coworkers against each other at work most.
The troublemaking got so bad that the team mood worsened.
I still don't know who stirred up the trouble.
Two friends had a big fight because of someone's scheming.

explain: 말 몇 마디로 두 사람 사이를 일부러 갈라놓는 나쁜 행동에 써요. '이간질(을) 하다', '이간질에 속다'처럼 쓰고, 좋은 뜻으로는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: It is used for the bad act of deliberately driving two people apart with a few words. It appears as '이간질(을) 하다' or '이간질에 속다' and is not used positively.

en: set people against each other; sow discord

examples.ko: 그 사람이 우리를 이간질해서 사이가 나빠졌어요.
examples.en: That person set us against each other, and our relationship soured.
Stay away from people who turn friends against each other.
You must not drive a couple apart with lies.
I really want to find out who stirred up the trouble.
There is someone going around sowing discord behind our backs.
Don't be shaken by words meant to split you up.

explain: 남의 사이를 일부러 나쁘게 만드는 일이에요. '~을/를 이간질하다', '두 사람을 이간질하다'로 써요. 같은 뜻의 '이간하다'는 주로 글에서 보여요.
explain_en: It means deliberately making a relationship between others go bad, used as '~을/를 이간질하다' or '두 사람을 이간질하다'. The same-meaning '이간하다' appears mostly in writing.
